one should likewise calculate the *mitya* for all the *salāna*. (62)
It should be joined with a secondary pedestal (upapīṭha), or it may be solely the left boar;
when divided into five parts, it is joined with a secondary pedestal.
The *adhiṣṭhāna* (base moulding) should have one part as the portion of Śiva, or two parts with the length of the *caraṇa* (foot-moulding);
the height of the *prastara* (coping) is one part when the *adhiṣṭhāna* consists of two parts.
One should fashion the *kumbhapīṭha* according to the sequence of the *upapīṭha*. Its height shall be declared as equal to its width and its base. (65)
The main temple (mūlaharmya) is declared to be four times [the size of the base],
while one should construct the gatehouse (gopura) to a measurement of five or six parts.
Having divided the width into eight parts, the wise one should plant [the pillars] in sequence, omitting one part each time, starting from the twelfth, tenth, and ninth parts.
It is proclaimed that [the measurement] multiplied by five, six, or seven parts is stated here as the width, extending from the hall (śālā) up to the gate-tower (gopura). 68.
Thus indeed is the measurement of the palace; now hear the measurement of the cubit (hasta) in its proper sequence, beginning from five cubits and increasing by two cubits at each step.
Just as a wise person should conceive it according to their faith,
so should one construct the fivefold [decoration] at the gate-tower (gopura) and arrange it in due order.
Beginning from seven cubits and increasing by one cubit at a time,
one should determine the measurement up to seventy cubits according to the desired proportion.
Beginning from nine cubits and increasing by two cubits at a time,
one should conceive of five types [of altars] ending at eighty-two cubits.
Beginning from the "Rudra" (eleven) cubit up to the "Aśiti" (eighty) cubit, one should determine the extent;
thus the width has been described. Now hear about the length from Madhu.
A wise person should fashion the height as one and a half feet, or one and a quarter feet, or even three-quarters of a foot; or it may be double, or even one and a half times that measure. (74)

One should cause the reduction or increase of eight, three-quarters, or half [the measurement], especially in the case of the width, for the sake of the auspiciousness of the length and other dimensions. (75)

Whether outside the square, in the middle of the square, or even within the square, one should determine the measurement there, provided that the first syllable (āyādi) is conjoined with an auspicious vowel.
The height should be conceived as equal to the width;
one should divide the width by six, and the wise one should determine the height by subtracting one part from that [sixth]. || 77 ||
In width, it should be nine parts, while the ornamentation is twelve parts;
the temple should be divided into three-quarters, and the excellent [structure] is double that.
One should construct the gatehouse (gopura) as either double or one-and-a-half times that [measurement],
extending from the northern direction up to the crest (śikhā), or alternatively, from the top of the head (mastaka).
One should draw out the side-chambers (kuṭaka) and so forth from the mind-line (mānasūtra) outward in sequence;
therein, the measurement of the pavilion (prāsāda) as stated [previously] is declared, and the Lord of Withdrawal (nivṛcceśa) is also described.
In one-third [of the width], two [parts] are thus; in one-fourth, two parts;
and in one-seventh, three parts—this indeed is the projection of the *sāla* (outer wall).
Starting from three cubits up to ten cubits,
one should likewise determine the width of the door in that same sequence.
The measurement of the door is prescribed as one and a half, or one and a quarter, or together with three quarters [of the width]; its height is twice that. || 83 ||

One should fashion the opening from two finger-breadths up to seven, starting from the middle of the *liṅga*; it should be situated to the left of the center of the *liṅga*, within the middle of the doorway. (84)
Beginning from twelve finger-breadths, it is traditionally held that [the measurement] extends up to fifty;
[this may be determined] by one-third, one part, or even one-fifth.
Thus, the pillar emerging from the base is elevated above the *dumbara* beam;
its measurement is equal to that of the door-pillar, extending from the *upanādi* to the end of the *uttara*.
The height of the door should be one-eighth [of the total], while the upapīṭhaka (sub-base) is one-fourth;
the adhiṣṭhāna (plinth) is two parts, and it should have a tilapāyana (a recessed joint) of two parts.
The *upapīṭha* (subsidiary pedestal) shall be one-eighth of the height, and the *triyaṃśaka* (triple-part) [the base] shall consist of three parts;
the height of the *adhiṣṭhāna* (plinth) shall be one-third of that [base]. || 88 ||
One should first determine the height of the pedestal (talipa) as two parts;
furthermore, the measurement of the location is prescribed as extending to the end of the emergence of the secondary pedestal (upapīṭha). || 89 ||
One should fashion the doorposts in the east and the west;
there should be a door-panel hinge in the east, but one should avoid it in the west.
Then, having duly described the yoga of the door-panels (kavaṭa) and the abode,
one should begin from the third row and extend it as far as the Rudra-row.
One should arrange either two rows or a single row as the measurement;
in a width divided into nine parts, the five-part section is for the *nāla* house.
The remaining portion shall be the width of the wall, or one may arrange it to be half of that;
the remainder, however, should be made the thickness of the wall for a single-storeyed building.
The width should be seven parts, and the length should likewise be so;
the inner chamber (garbhagṛha) shall consist of three parts, and the thickness of the wall shall be one part.

The *karṇakūṭa* of the portion belonging to Śiva should be two parts, free from deception; its width and length should likewise be two parts each, with an interval for the *hāra* (necklace) of two parts.
The [temple] known as Dvitāla has been described; now Tritāla is being discussed.
One should divide the length into ten parts, and the width should be the same.
The inner sanctum (garbhageha) shall consist of three parts; the pedestal for the deity (grahapiṇḍikā) one part;
the portico (ālindra) two parts; and the width of the frieze (hārāvyāsa) nine parts.
The *karṇakūṭa* is one part of Śiva; the length of the *śālā* is three parts;
its width is one part; the *pañcaravi* is half a part; and the distance between the two *hari*s is half a part.
In this very manner, by the same sequence, the *dvitāla* should be as described before;
the *tritāla* is renowned as being twice that, so now hear about the four-storey [temple] below.
Starting from one and ending with the square of the yugas (four), excluding the wall [measurement],
it extends from two tālas up to a kalā, combined with three and a half crores.
One part, or half, or one and a half crores in extent, joined with a portion of the central cell—this is the Subhadraka of one and a half crores. || 101 ||
In the width, one part out of eleven is for the neck (nāla), three parts out of nine are for the house (geh),
two parts are for the thickness of the wall (bhitti), and by one part, the supporting beam (dhārika) should be formed.
Then, half a part [of the width] is declared to be the outer wall, extending across the expanse of the necklace;
having divided the width into ten parts, one part is for the corner pinnacle (karṇakūṭa).
The long rectangle of the cell and so forth consists of four parts; the remainder is the *hārasapañjara*.
Having omitted one part for the corner pinnacle (*karṇakūṭa*), this applies especially to the length. (104)
Then, having divided [the width] into sixteen parts, two parts shall be the side cell;
the length of the hall shall be six parts, while the penthouse (pañjara) shall be half a part.
The remainder is declared to be another *hāra* (necklace) in this very same sequence;
the stalk (*nāla*) should be thirteen parts in width, and the house (*geha*) three parts.
In one part there is a triple-piṇḍa; by another part, the aṇḍānika should be formed. One part is for the length of the necklace (hāra), and it constitutes the width of the outer wall.
The one most skilled in ritual design should fashion [the structure] from the level of the *rasa* (six) up to the level of the *bhūmi* (eight),
with a width of twelve finger-breadths for one part, and the *kūṭa* (nine) being forgotten.

The length of the central bay (koṣṭha) shall be five parts; the remainder is for the necklace (hārā) and the lattice-work (sapañjara). Having omitted one part from the corner-ridge (karṇakūṭa), this is especially [applied] to the longitudinal extent (āyāma). || 109 ||
The length of the hall is divided into seven parts; the remainder constitutes the frieze and the lattice-work.
This is known as the "Six-Earth" (rasabhūmi) type, and now the "Seven-Earth" (saptabhūmi) type is described.
Having divided [the length] into thirteen parts, one part shall be the width of the kūṭa;
the length of the hall shall be five parts, and the remainder shall be the space for the garlands (hārāntara). || 111 ||
Having set aside the portion of the ear-protrusion (karṇakūṭa), specifically regarding the length,
the length should be twenty-three parts, while the length of the inner courtyard (koṣṭha) should be six parts.

The side-chamber (pārśvakoṣṭha) consists of two parts, the lattice-work (pañjara) consists of one part, and the remainder is joined with the necklace (hāra); this is known as the seven-storied [temple]. || 113 ||
Having performed the expansion as before, one part is for the corner-pinnacle (karṇakūṭaka),
five parts are for the hall (śālā), and the remainder is for the frieze with its lattice-work (hārasapañjara).
In the length, however, one should specifically omit the portion of the ear-protrusion;
likewise, from the twenty-three parts, one should omit two parts for the two side-cells.

The length of the hall shall be divided into seven parts; the penthouse (pañjara) shall consist of one and a half parts, the inner chamber (koṣṭha) shall be one part more [than that], and the remainder shall be the decorative frieze (hārā) together with the penthouse.
Excluding the portion of the *karṇakūṭa*, the length is thus determined.
In this manner, the inner sanctum (*garbhagṛha*) extends from the sixth part up to the earth-limit, consisting of three parts.
The remainder, as previously described, is said to extend up to the ninth stage; this is the *pañjara*. 118.

The remainder is declared to be another necklace, known as the nine-tiered (navabhūmi). Seventeen parts of the width [of the base] constitute the width of the pinnacle (kūṭa), which is one part. || 119 ||
The length of the central bay should be seven parts; the remainder shall be the necklace and the lattice-work.
Thus, the length is thirty-two [parts], while each side bay is two parts.
The compartment (koṣṭha) should thus be one-tenth [of the total], while the lattice-work (pañjara) is made with half that portion;
the remainder is declared to be the space between the necklaces (hārāntara); in this manner, one should fashion the ten-storied structure.
In the total width, one part is for the corner-ridge (karṇakūṭaka), two parts are for the side-cell (pārśvakoṣṭha), and six parts are for the length of the cell (koṣṭhadairghya). || 122 ||
The width of the cage (pañjara) should be half a part, while the remaining space up to the neck-chain (hārāntara) is considered the length;
thus it should be constructed, excluding the portion for the corner-pinnacle (karṇakūṭa).
In the length, however, there should be two parts; the longitudinal compartment should be eight parts.
The side compartment should be one-fifth part, and the cage-like structure (pañjara) should be three-quarters [of that]. || 124 ||
The remainder is declared to be another necklace (hārāntara), known as the "ground of Rudra" (rudrabhūmi).
The length of the cage (pañjara) should be one, a half, or three-quarters [of that]. || 125 ||
The remainder is declared to be the space for the necklaces; one should arrange it according to the rule.
It consists of seventy-three divisions, of which one part is for the ear-ornament (karṇakūṭaka).
One part in eight is for the side compartments, and one part in ten is for the central compartment;
half a part is declared for the lattice-work (pañjara), and the remainder is known as the space between the necklaces (hārāntara). || 127 ||
The length [of the hall] shall be thirty-eight parts, and the side compartment two parts; the length of the hall shall be twelve parts, and the penthouse (pañjara) shall be nine parts.
It is declared to be equal to the remaining necklace (śeṣahāra) and is known as the "land of Karka";
its width is three parts plus a twentieth part, and the width of the peak (kūṭa) is one part.

The side-chamber (pārśvakoṣṭha) is two parts, the corner-chamber (koṣṭha) is ten parts, and the penthouse (pañjara) is said to be one part; thus, it is described as having thirteen stories in sequence.

The width is twenty-two parts, and one part is the width of the pinnacle (kūṭa). The length of the hall (śālā) is eleven parts, while the two side chambers (pārśvakoṣṭha) are two parts each. || 131 ||
The remaining portion of the work should be performed with five parts; the garlands should be equal.
Then, having divided four parts, one should likewise make a square cell of twelve parts. (132)
The side chamber (pārśvakoṣṭha) consists of two parts, while the area for worship is half a part;
the remainder is the interval between the necklaces (hārāntara), and this is considered the fourteen-story structure.
The width should be nine parts, while the *viśada* portion is one part; the *karṇakūṭaka* is nine parts, and likewise the *kūṭa* is two parts for each of the two side compartments. || 134 ||
Half a part is declared to be the cage (pañjara), and the remainder is the space for the necklaces; specifically, in terms of length, it should indeed consist of fifty parts.
The central compartment (koṣṭha) is one-twentieth [of the width], the side compartments (pārśvakoṣṭhaka) are two parts,
the lattice-work (pañjara) is said to be three-quarters, and the remainder is the space for the necklaces (hārāntara), in sequence.
The width [of the temple] is twenty-nine parts; the width of the pinnacle (kūṭa) is one part;
the two side compartments are two parts each, and the central compartment is ten parts.

One part is declared to be the cage (pañjara), and the remainder is known as the interval between the necklaces (hārāntara). One should divide that [remainder] into sixty parts; therein, the central square consists of thirteen parts.

The side-chamber (pārśvakoṣṭha) shall be two parts, and the cage (pañjara) one part; the remainder is declared to be the space between the garlands (hārāntara). This is the supreme measurement for elephants. || 139 ||
Now hear about the entry into the five levels and so forth upon the sacrificial mound (*prasthara*).
A wise man should prepare the *prasthara* as either *subhadra* or *vibhadra*. (140)
In this manner, the Bhadra [type] of the Kaṇyakūṭa and other halls is prescribed;
now I shall describe the measurement of the Gaṇḍa, so listen to that, O Prabhañjana! || 141 ||
One should fashion the ground portion starting from the *ukta* (the base) up to the *śikhā* (the pinnacle);
the height of the *kapota* (dove-cot cornice) should be one and a half parts, and the *gala* (neck) should be one part.
On a pinnacle that is one-quarter less than thirty [units], the remaining part is the spire (śikhara);
in this very sequence, it is known as the single-storeyed (ekabhauma) temple.
From the north to the crest [of the pinnacle], it is remembered as the "portion of Nanda" (nine parts).
One part is the measure of five, while the pitcher consists of one and a half portions. (144)
The crest (śikhā) should be made remaining as a remnant, and the two tiers (dvitala) should be arranged according to the sequence;
from the north to the end of the crest, it should indeed consist of thirteen parts.
The bedframe (mañca) should measure one and a half parts, the feet (adhraka) one and two-quarter parts;
the height of the molding (prastara) one and a quarter parts, and the base (pāda) two parts. || 146 ||
The height of the pigeon (kapota) should be one part; its base and the neck are equal to that.
The śaka is said to be one and a half parts; the remainder is known as the udaya.
From the north to the crest, divided into nine parts,
the measurement is five parts, one and a quarter parts, two parts, and one-quarter part in length.
The *kapota* (dove-cornice) is one part of Śiva (eleven parts), and the *śiras* (crown) is one and a half parts of a *pakṣa* (eight parts);
the remainder is declared to be the pair of *stūpīs*. This is known as the two-storeyed (*dvitala*) *jvī*. || 149 ||
From the northern edge to the top of the spire, when divided into thirteen parts,
the measurement shall be five and a half parts, and its height shall be two and a half parts plus one-quarter.
The height of the *kapota* (dove-cornice) is one and a quarter parts; its wings are one part, and its length is one quarter.
The measurement of the *mañca* (pedestal) is one part, and the neck (*gala*) is said to be one-sixteenth of a part. 151.
The pinnacle (śikhara) should be one and a half parts; the remainder shall be the height of the plinth (udaya).
Thus the three-tiered (tritala) [structure] is described; now hear concerning the four-storeyed (caturbhūmi) [structure]. || 152 ||
In the *Sthūpīyottarasiddhānta*, [the height] is divided into ten parts;
the base is two parts, the neck is one part, the capital is two parts, and the width of the wings is four parts. (153)
The portion of the sky (vyomāṃśa) shall be the measure for the platform (mañca), and the neck (gala) is said to be equal to that.
The pinnacle (śikhara) shall be twenty-seven [units] less a quarter, and the remainder shall constitute the finial (sthūpī) and so forth. || 154 ||
This is declared to be the four-fold stage; now hear about the stage of the arrow (bāṇabhūmi).
From the north to the top-knot (śikhā), it consists of twenty-five divisions.
The wing-section should be equal to the height of the platform (mañca), with its height being one and a half parts plus a quarter;
the height of the *kapota* (dove-cot) should be one and a quarter parts, and its length should be three parts. || 156 ||
The height of the pedestal (mañca) should be one and a half parts; the height of the base (adhi) should be one and a half parts of a pakṣa;
the height of the kapiśīrṣaka (dormer) should be one and a quarter parts; and its length should be one part of a pakṣa.
The height of the *kapota* (dove-cot) is said to be one and a half parts, with its projection being equal to that;
the height of the *śikhara* (spire) is four parts, and the remainder shall be for the *sthūpī* (finial) and other elements. 158.
The five stages have been declared; now the stage of taste (rasabhūmi) is described:
from the northern direction to the crest (śikhā), it consists of thirty-one degrees. || 159 ||
The height of the pedestal with its plinth is two and a quarter parts; the length of the sanctuary is eight parts;
the measurement of the couch is one-eighth part, while its height is one and a half parts.
The height of the seat (mañca) is one and three-quarter parts; its length for the movable [pedestal] is seven parts;
the measurement of the seat itself is four and a half parts, while the height of the feet is two and a half parts. || 161 ||
The height of the *kapota* (dove-cornice) is one and a quarter parts; its width is one-sixteenth part, and its length is one-fourth part.
The measurement of the *mañca* (pedestal) is one-ninth part, while the projection of the *gala* (neck) is one and a quarter parts.
The pinnacle (śikhara) shall consist of two parts, and the remainder shall be the stūpikā and so forth;
this is declared to be the six-storeyed [temple]. Now hear concerning the seven-storeyed [temple]. || 163 ||
And from the north to the crest, it is divided into thirty-eight parts.
The height [of the base] is two and a half parts, the projection (utseka) is one part;
the height of the pillar (pāda) is four and a quarter parts, and the height of the capital (uccha) is two and a quarter parts, with its length being four parts. || 164 ||
The height of the wall (mañca) shall be one-fifth of the width, while mine (the temple) shall be half of that; the height of the base (tuṅga) shall be one-fourth of that;
the height of the entablature (mañcocca) shall be one and a quarter parts; and its length shall be one-fourth of the width. || 165 ||

The height of the wings, shoulders, and hips should be one *yuga* (two cubits), while the height from the feet to the top of the pillar (*sthāṇu*) should be three-quarters of a *matta*. Half of that is the depth of the submerged part, which is one *tāla*. || 166 ||
The height of the pedestal (mañca) shall be one and a half parts, while the plinth (pāda) shall be thirty parts plus a quarter.
The height of the cornice (kapota) is one and a quarter parts, and the neck (gala) is said to be three parts. || 167 ||
In the fifth part of the pinnacle (śikhara), the remainder shall be the stūpī and so forth;
this is declared to be the seven-storied [temple]. Now hear concerning the eight-storied one from below.
Having divided the portion into five parts, one should increase it by two; the planet extends to that end. It has two feet, two-fifths of a part, half a sixth, and a measure of half a sesame seed.
The height of the pedestal (mañca) is two and one-quarter parts; its width is one part;
its depth is two and one-quarter parts; the height of the architrave (ūrdhva) is four-eighths (one-half); and its length is four parts. || 170 ||
The height of the base (mañca) should be one-fifth [of the total], while the height of the pedestal (aṅghri) is one-fourth;
the height of the architrave (añcorca) is two-fifths less a quarter, and its length is three and a half times the height of the pedestal.
The height of the pedestal (mañca) should be one and a half parts, while the height of the legs (aṅghri) should be double that;
the height of the cornice (kapota) should be one and a quarter parts, and the length of the wings (pakṣa) should be half the length of the legs.

One and a quarter parts is said to be the *kapota* (dove-cot), one-third part the *gala* (neck), and at the pinnacle (*śikhara*), five parts are for the remainder, which constitutes the *sthūpī* (finial) and so forth. || 173 ||
That which is called the "earth of Vasu" has been declared; now hear about the "earth of Nanda" below.
Then, one should divide it into six parts, starting from the north and ending at the crest. (174)
The *mañca* (platform) is two parts out of three, twice as high [as the pillar-base], half the height of the *bhūta*, and one-fourth the length of the foot;
the *kapota* (eave-cornice) is two parts out of three, with a projection of fifty units. || 175 ||
The platform (mañca) should be two and one-quarter parts, the base (tali) four parts in length, and the pedestal (prastara) two parts;
likewise, for the sake of the fire-altar, it should be three parts in length.
The height of the *kapota* (dove-cornice) should be three parts; its width [the length of the base] should be three parts; the measure of the *añcana* (projection) should be one and a half parts;
and the length of the *śaraṇa* (porch) should be two and a half parts. || 177 ||
The height of the *kapota* (dove-cornice) is one and a quarter parts; its width is two parts.
The measurement of the *prastara* (beam) is one part, while the neck (*gala*) is said to be three parts.
In the fifth part of the pinnacle (śikhara), the remainder shall constitute the stūpikā and so forth;
from the northern direction to the end of the pinnacle, it shall consist of sixty-four parts.

The height of the throne is thirty-one and a quarter units, while its elevation is half and a quarter of a *kauśika* unit; the measurement of the seat is three parts, and the pedestal is four and a half parts. (180)
The mañca (pedestal) is one and three-quarter parts; the ūrdhva (upper part) is one-fifth;
the talipa (plinth) is one part; the kapota (cornice) is one and a half parts; and the aghri (base) is one and a quarter parts. || 181 ||
The height of the mañca is two and one-quarter parts, its width is four parts, and its length is one part;
the height of the kapota is one and one-quarter parts, and the gala is said to be equal to that. || 182 ||
At the peak, occupying two parts, the remainder shall be for the *sthūpī* and so forth;
this is declared to be the ten-fold stage (*daśabhūmi*). Now hear about the eleven-fold stage (*rudrabhūmi*) below. (183)
The height of the *kapota* (dove-cornice) is seventy parts from the north to the top of the *śikhara*, plus one and a half parts of fire (*agni*, three); the *talipa* is six and a half [parts]. (184)

The height of the mañca (platform) is three and one-quarter parts; the height of the *kauśika* (the base of the pillar) is one-fourth part; the height of the *kapota* (dove-cornice) is three parts, and its thickness is four and a half parts. 185.
The height of the mañca (pedestal) is three parts less a quarter; its width is five parts;
the kapota (cornice) is one and a half parts; and the foot (aghrīka) is four and a quarter parts.

The height of the pedestal (mañca) is two and one-quarter [parts], its width is four parts, and its length is one part; the measurement of the pedestal is five parts, and its height is four and a half parts.
The height of the pedestal (mañca) is one and three-quarter parts, its width is one part, and its length is one-quarter part;
the measurement of the pedestal is one and a half parts, while the height of the base (adhraka) is one and a quarter parts.
The height of the *kapota* (dove-cornice) is one and a quarter parts; its width is one-sixteenth part, and its length is one-fourth [of the total].
The measurement of the *mañca* (platform) is one and a quarter parts, and the *gala* (neck) is said to be equal to that.
The pinnacle (śikhara) should be one-fourth of the [total] height; the remainder shall consist of the dome (sthūpī) and other elements.
This is declared to be the "earth of Rudra" (eleven parts); now hear about the "earth of the Sun" (twelve parts).
The height from the northern direction to the top of the crest is fifty-five parts;
the height of the *mañca* is two and three-quarters parts, and its width is one and three-quarter parts. || 191 ||
The height of the *kapota* (dove-cornice) is one and a half parts; the *varaṇa* (enclosure) is six and a half parts;
the height of the *mañca* (platform) is three and a quarter parts; and its length is six parts.
The height of the *kapota* (dove-cornice) should be one part; the *guṇa* (moulding) one-third part;
the *pāda* (base) one and a half parts; the *añca* (projection) three parts; and the length of the *tali* (pedestal) five parts.
The height of the pedestal (mañca) is one and a half parts; the height of the base (adhi) is four and a half parts;
the height of the pedestal (mañca) is two and a quarter parts; and the length of the plinth (caraṇa) is four parts. || 194 ||
The wing-section (pakṣāṃśa) should be the measure for the dais (mañca), with a height of three and a half parts plus one-quarter;
the height of the dais should be one and three-quarters parts, and its length should be three parts.

The height of the pedestal (mañca) is one and a half parts, the height of the base (adhi) is one and a half parts, the height of the pigeon-ornament (kapota) is one and a quarter parts, and the length of the plinth (caraṇa) is one part. || 196 ||
The *mañca* (pedestal) shall be one part together with a quarter-part, and the *gala* (neck) shall be equal to that;
the *śikhara* (spire) shall be four parts, and the remainder shall consist of the *sthūpī* (finial) and so forth. || 197 ||
Listen to the description of the thirteenth floor, called Bhānubhūmi;
from the northern direction to the crest, it consists of ninety-six divisions. (198)
The height of the pedestal (mañca) should be one-sixteenth of the [total] measurement, while the height of the base (aṅghri) should be five and a half parts;
the height of the pedestal (mañca) should be three-quarters of that, and its width should be equal to the length of the foot (caraṇa). || 199 ||
The height of the *kapota* (dove-cot) is one and a half *tālīpas*; the *talipa* is six and a half;
the height of the *mañca* (platform) is three-quarters with a quarter added; and its length is six parts. || 200 ||
The height of the platform (mañca) should be one part out of nine; the height of the pedestal (aṅghrika) should be five and a half parts;
the height of the platform (mañcocca) should be two and three-quarter parts; and the length of the base (caraṇa) should be four parts. || 201 ||
The *kapota* (dove-cornice) should have a height of one and a half parts, with a base of four and a half parts;
its *añca* (projection) should be two and a quarter parts high, and its length at the base should be four parts. || 202 ||
The foot is two parts, the thigh is three parts, and the length of the leg is one part. || 203 ||
The height of the pedestal (mañca) is one and a half parts; the height of the base (adhi) is one and a half parts of a quarter-part (pakṣāṃśa);
the height of the pedestal (mañca) is one and a quarter parts; and the length of the foot (caraṇa) is one quarter-part. || 204 ||
One part is for the auspicious base (śivāṃśa), and one and a quarter parts is the height of the neck (galodaya);
the pinnacle (śikhara) is two parts, and the remainder shall be for the finial (sthūpī) and so forth. || 205 ||
The thirteenth level has been described; now hear concerning the ground of Manu, which consists of one hundred and eight [squares], extending from the north to the top-knot (śikhā).
The height of the seat, including the pedestal, should be eight parts; the length of the foot should be four parts;
the measurement of the seat itself should be four parts; and the foot [of the pillar] should be seven and a half parts.
The height of the *agni* (fire) part is three-quarters [of the unit]; the height of the *mañca* (platform) is seven parts; the length of the *caraṇa* (base) is one-quarter;
the height of the *kapota* (dove-cot) is one and a half parts; and the *talipa* (pedestal) is six and a half parts.
The height of the pedestal (mañca) is three and one-quarter parts; its width is six parts;
the measurement of the seat (añca) is three parts, while the foot (aṅghri) is four and a half parts.
The height of the pedestal (mañca) is three parts less a quarter; its width is five parts, and its length is one part.
Its projection is one and a half parts, and the plinth (aghrīka) is likewise one and a half parts.
The height of the pedestal (mañca) is two and a quarter parts, its width is four parts, and its length is one part.
The foot (pāda) is not [equal to] two parts; the height of the pedestal is three parts, and its length is two parts.
The measurement of the pedestal is one and a half parts, while the height of the foot is one and a half parts.
The feet should be extended comfortably, and the neck should be held straight, level with the shoulders. || 213 ||
The pinnacle (śikhara) shall consist of four parts of the Vedas (four units), while the remainder shall be the stūpī and so forth.
This is declared to be the "ground of Manmatha. Now hear [the description] of the "ground of Tithi" below. (214)
The twenty-first [digit] ends at the hundred;
the fifth measure is a portion of the yuga, while the feet consist of a portion of half a fortnight.
The height of the seat with the feet included is one-eighth [of the total height], its depth is one-sixteenth, and the height of the seat itself is one-fourth;
it has seven and a half parts for the legs.
The height of the *tripāda* (three-quarter) portion is three and a half units;
the height of the *kapota* (dove-cornice) is one and a half units; and the *talipa* (plinth) is six and a half units. || 217 ||
The height of the pinnacle (ucca) is three and one-quarter parts, and the tilapāyita is six parts; the measurement of the architrave (añca) is three parts, while the pedestal (pādika) is [one part].
The height of the pedestal (mañca) is three-quarters less one-third [of the base], and the height of the plinth (bhūta) is one-fifth plus one-quarter.
